title: 2026 U.S. House General Election — Texas's 8th Congressional District
description: An open-seat race for Texas's 8th Congressional District, as two-term Republican incumbent Morgan Luttrell is retiring. The district covers the northern Houston exurbs — including portions of Montgomery, Harris, Waller, and Walker counties — and has a strong Republican lean (Cook PVI R+13, with Donald Trump winning it by over 30 points in 2024). Republican nominee Jessica Steinmann, a former Trump Justice Department official and Ted Cruz aide, easily won the March 3, 2026 primary with 68% of the vote. Democratic nominee Laura Jones, a small business owner and Army mom, won her primary with 66%. Given the district's partisan makeup, Steinmann is considered the heavy favorite in the general election.
polling_note: No district-specific opinion polls were found for Texas's 8th Congressional District in 2026. Statewide generic-ballot polls from the Texas Politics Project and Texas A&M/ReconMR showed Republican leads of 1–6 points, but these are not precinct-level and do not reflect TX-08 specifically.

candidates.name: Jessica Steinmann
candidates.summary: Jessica Hart Steinmann is an attorney and former Trump administration official who won the Republican nomination for Texas's 8th Congressional District. She served as Director of the Office for Victims of Crime at the U.S. Department of Justice and later as Executive General Counsel of the America First Policy Institute. She previously worked for U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, helped draft Texas's 2021 election integrity law, and has been endorsed by President Donald Trump, Senator Ted Cruz, and Governor Greg Abbott.

candidates.name: Laura Jones
candidates.summary: Laura Jones is a lifelong Texan, Army mom, small business owner, and farmer who won the Democratic nomination for Texas's 8th Congressional District. A real estate broker by profession and a former county chair, she has run for office multiple times and describes herself as a working-class candidate focused on kitchen-table economic issues. Her platform includes raising the federal minimum wage and tying it to the cost of living, expanding Medicare for All, and increasing taxes on billionaires and large corporations to fund affordable housing, education, and infrastructure.
